proof_nl: Let T_k(q) = [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k. Then, by definition, F_{d,r,n}(q) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} T_k(q). For k=0, each q-Pochhammer factor with subscript 0 is an empty product, hence equals 1. Therefore (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_0 = 1, (q^d;q^d)_0 = 1, and (q^{2d};q^{2d})_0 = 1; also q^{0(d-d*0-2r)/2} = 1 and [3d*0+r]_q = [r]_q. So T_0(q) = [r]_q. Consequently, F_{d,r,n}(q) - R_{d,r,n}(q) = T_0(q) + sum_{k=1}^{n-1} T_k(q) - R_{d,r,n}(q) = ([r]_q - R_{d,r,n}(q)) + sum_{k=1}^{n-1} T_k(q). By the definitions of the modified summands, H_{d,r,n,0}(q) = [r]_q - R_{d,r,n}(q), and for every k with 1 <= k <= n-1 we have H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_k(q). Hence F_{d,r,n}(q) - R_{d,r,n}(q) = H_{d,r,n,0}(q) + sum_{k=1}^{n-1} H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} H_{d,r,n,k}(q). This is exactly the stated identity.
solver_summary: Split the defining sum for F into its k=0 term and the terms k>=1. The k=0 term equals [r]_q because every q-Pochhammer with subscript 0 is 1. After subtracting R, the resulting expression is exactly H_0 plus the unchanged summands H_k for 1<=k<=n-1.

By the stated definitions of H_{d,r,n,0} and H_{d,r,n,k} for k>=1, this is exactly the claimed identity. The argument matches the lemma's intended role as a repackaging step and uses no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
